text: Ethical intuitionism (Ross, Audi) characterizes basic moral knowledge as:
choices: self-evident and known non-inferentially - grasped by rational insight without being derived from other beliefs, on the model of a priori knowledge.
justified by its coherence with our other moral and non-moral beliefs, reached by mutually adjusting particular judgments and general principles.
not truth-apt at all, since moral utterances merely express attitudes or emotions rather than describe any facts.
a construction out of what fully rational agents would agree to, so that there are no mind-independent moral facts waiting to be grasped.
explanation: Intuitionism holds that some moral propositions (for example, that cruelty is wrong) are self-evident and known directly, without inference, structurally like a priori insight. Coherentist reflective equilibrium (1) is the rival justificatory structure; expressivism (2) denies that moral claims are truth-apt; and constructivism (3) makes moral facts procedure-dependent rather than objects of non-inferential rational insight.
